- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 2–5% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If official event net supply is negative and sentiment is bearish, model often underestimates downside; add 3–8% downward bias to forecast mean.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated bearish swings (e.g., -0.50 or -1.00), model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–3 days ahead to align with sentiment decay.  
- For 30-day forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model often overestimates bullishness; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent 18-day average to avoid overconfidence.  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.33), model tends to drift toward recent mean; apply mean reversion to forecast by 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
